name: Pearson correlation coefficient
definition: The covariance of two paired samples divided by the product of their standard deviations: the sum of products of deviations from each sample's mean, over the square root of the product of the sums of squared deviations. It lies between -1 and 1, is symmetric, and doesn't change under a positive linear transformation of either sample.
citations: John A. Rice, Mathematical Statistics and Data Analysis, 3rd edition, Duxbury, 2007, section 4.3.
Larry Wasserman, All of Statistics, Springer, 2004, section 3.3.

call.inputs: two paired one-dimensional samples of equal length

properties.says: A sample against twice itself gives 1.
A sample against a reversed linear copy gives -1.
Scaling and shifting a sample doesn't change the coefficient.
Swapping the samples doesn't change the coefficient.

provenance.why: Chosen as a common numeric or text method from general knowledge, before any retained workspace was surveyed for candidates.
